chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah, who said:

I wrote to the Righteous Slave (peace be upon him), 'If our Master deems it appropriate to inform me, (I would like to know) about the best rewards for the Ziyarah of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and whether it equals the reward of Hajj for those who have missed it.' He (peace be upon him) wrote back, 'It equals Hajj for those who have missed Hajj.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for Ziyarah of Imam Husayn compared to Hajj?
ai.summary: In this correspondence, Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah queries Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) regarding the supreme merit of Ziyarat al-Husayn, to which the Imam replies that it equals the reward of Hajj for those unable to perform it. This specific ruling highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia piety, positioning the visitation of the martyrs as a substitute for the obligatory pilgrimage when circumstances prevent travel. It underscores the concept that spiritual proximity to the Imams carries weight comparable to major acts of worship.
